messages.subject: bi factor model questions
parts:
Hello, 

Just a general question on running bifactor model. 
I realised that using the bfactor() doesn't allow one to change the method type to "MHRM". 

So I did something like this: 

specific <- c(rep(1,5), rep(2,6),rep(3,6),rep(4,5),rep(5,6),rep(6,6),rep(7,5))
mod1 <- bfactor(d1sa, specific, technical = list(NCYCLES = 2000))

But under the example from the mirt(), it shows a bifactor model could be conducted like this: 

#bifactor (mirt) ####
model.3 <- '
G = 1-39
F1 = 1-5
F2 = 6-11
F3 = 12-17
F4 = 18-22
F5 = 23-28
F6 = 29-34
F7 = 35-39
'
bimod <- mirt(d1sa,model.3, method = 'MHRM', itemtype="graded") 

Is there any reason why the bfactor() can't change the estimator? 
Or under what conditions should I consider using the 'MHRM' instead? 

Thank you, 
Aiden

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: bi factor model questions
parts:
See the associated reference in ?bfactor to see how/why bfactor() behaves the way it does:

Cai, L. (2010). A two-tier full-information item factor analysis model with applications. Psychometrika, 75, 581-612.

Chalmers, R., P. (2012). mirt: A Multidimensional Item Response Theory Package for the R Environment. Journal of Statistical Software, 48(6), 1-29. doi: 10.18637/jss.v048.i06

Gibbons, R. D., & Hedeker, D. R. (1992). Full-information Item Bi-Factor Analysis. Psychometrika, 57, 423-436.

Gibbons, R. D., Darrell, R. B., Hedeker, D., Weiss, D. J., Segawa, E., Bhaumik, D. K., Kupfer, D. J., Frank, E., Grochocinski, V. J., & Stover, A. (2007). Full-Information item bifactor analysis of graded response data. Applied Psychological Measurement, 31, 4-19.

Phil
